title: A DD statement that names the PATH over an alternate index, next to the DD for the base cluster
shapes: AIXA jcl/AIXARUN.jcl KSD010: //ORDKSD DD DSN=PROD.AIXA.ORDER,DISP=OLD and //ORDKSD1 DD DSN=PROD.AIXA.ORDER.PATH,DISP=OLD
asserts: Step KSD010 has two jcl_dds facts: ORDKSD on the base cluster PROD.AIXA.ORDER and ORDKSD1 on PROD.AIXA.ORDER.PATH, the path defined by H-0079. The path is a data set name in the catalog, not a data set of its own on a volume: the DD does not name the alternate index PROD.AIXA.ORDER.AIX. The COBOL program names only ORDKSD in its SELECT; the alternate index is identified in the program solely by the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Programming Guide (SC27-8714-03)
citations.quote: In your COBOL program, the alternate index is identified solely by the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause in the FILE-CONTROL paragraph.
